title: Dublin vs London: Which Should You Visit?
verdict: If you crave intimate pub culture, friendly banter, and a more manageable city footprint, Dublin is your winner with a comfortable daily budget of €150-250 ($160-270). faq.question: Which city is better for a first-time international traveler?
faq.answer: London might be slightly easier for a first-timer due to its extensive public transport, clearer signage, and the sheer volume of information available. However, Dublin's smaller size and welcoming vibe can also make it less overwhelming, depending on your comfort level.

faq.question: How many days should I spend in each city?
faq.answer: For Dublin, 3-4 full days are ideal to see the main sights and enjoy the pub scene. For London, you really need at least 5-7 days to scratch the surface and experience its diverse neighborhoods and attractions without rushing too much.

faq.question: Is public transport easy to use in both cities?
faq.answer: Yes, both cities have excellent public transport. Dublin's buses and Luas tram are straightforward, especially with a Leap Card. London's Tube and bus network are extensive and efficient, best navigated with an Oyster card or contactless payment, though it can feel more complex due to its size.

faq.question: What are the language differences?
faq.answer: Both cities primarily speak English. While Ireland has Irish (Gaelic) as its first official language, English is universally spoken. You'll encounter a vast array of accents in both, but communication will be easy for English speakers.

faq.question: Are the cities safe for tourists?
faq.answer: Both Dublin and London are generally safe for tourists. Like any major city, exercise common sense, be aware of your surroundings, especially at night, and watch out for pickpockets in crowded tourist areas. Public transport is safe in both.

faq.question: Can I use the same currency in both?
faq.answer: No. Dublin uses the Euro (€), while London uses the British Pound (£). You will need to exchange currency or use separate debit/credit cards for each country. Many places accept contactless payments.

faq.question: What's the weather like, and when's the best time to visit?
faq.answer: Both cities have temperate maritime climates, meaning changeable weather year-round with frequent rain. Summer (June-August) offers the warmest temperatures and longest daylight hours, but also peak crowds. Spring (April-May) and Autumn (Sept-Oct) offer pleasant weather and fewer tourists.

faq.question: Which city is better for families with kids?
faq.answer: London likely offers more dedicated attractions for families, from the London Eye and Harry Potter Studios to numerous parks and interactive museums (many free). Dublin has some great family options like Dublin Zoo and Viking Splash Tour, but London has a broader range of child-friendly activities.
